_hinweis: English texts of the dressing-room stories (kb_*).

standard: You're the DJ – one hour a week.
I'll bring a list! And maybe a fog machine.
Everyone picks one song. In turn.
In turn is fair. I'll take the ballad then – just kidding.
Before the game it's quiet. Full stop.
Silence? Like at the dentist. Understood, Coach.
{spieler_kurz}: The playlist war

Coach, there's a war going on in the dressing room: I want pop ballads, the lads want bass. Yesterday the same song played three times in a row. I'm thinking of wearing headphones – or bringing my own cable.
I'll sing along – badly but loudly.
Then the ritual stays. And I'll finally learn the chorus.
Nice. But it stops before kick-off.
Understood. Short, loud, over.
The dressing room sings along
Since {spieler_kurz} got to choose the music, half the squad sings along on the way out. The keeper knows every verse, just not the chorus.
Music is allowed again – quietly.
Quietly is enough. Even the kit man is bobbing along.
The silence stays.
As you wish. We'll listen to breathing then.
Dressing room, no signal
Since the pre-match silence all you hear is studs clicking. {spieler_kurz} hums secretly in the shower. The mood is … quiet.
Scene: The dressing-room hit
Before kick-off a song plays that nobody wants to have chosen. Everyone sings. You too, Coach – we heard you.
That stays between us.
Keep them. But wash them first.
Thanks! I'll wash them – in spirit.
You have luck or you don't. Socks don't matter.
Hm. I'll put a second pair in. To be safe.
Fresh socks. Now.
Now? Do you know what that does to the karma?
{spieler_kurz} and the lucky socks
Coach, I have a confession: since the away win I've worn the same socks. The laundry lady is getting nervous, so am I. May I carry on, or is that going too far?
At least it smells of success.
The best thing about the run: nobody sits next to me.
The washing machine is next door. Use it.
Will do. With ceremony.
The socks keep winning
The run continues, so do the socks. The kit man and the physio have a bet on when they will walk off on their own.
Fine, wear them again. Washed once a week.
Once a week! A compromise I can live with.
The decision stands.
Fine. With a headache, then.
The sock dispute
Since the ban {spieler_kurz} plays visibly stiffer. He says the new socks are 'too tight in the head'. The physio recommends a talk.
Scene: The last sock
In the cup tie a single sock hangs on the corner flag. Nobody admits hanging it there. We win the game anyway.
We don't ask.
I'll talk to both of you. Together.
Together is good. With coffee? I'll bring the coffee.
Whoever is out hands the armband in. Done.
Clear rule, clear heads. Thanks.
Armbands are a side issue.
A side issue. Of course. For you, maybe.
{spieler_kurz} and the armband
Coach, I'm glad to be vice-captain. But when the skipper is out he still wears the armband for an hour after the match. I have nothing against him. Just against armbands on arms that aren't mine.
That's mature. Thanks, both of you.
We even took a photo. For the archive.
Good. Back to training.
Back to it. With hook.
Peace in the armband row
The skipper and {spieler_kurz} have agreed: the armband will hang on a hook in the dressing room, with a name tag and washing instructions.
I'll sit you at one table.
At one table? Fine, if there's cake.
Sort it out between you.
We'll sort it. Probably not.
Cold war at the hook
{spieler_kurz} and the skipper only greet each other with hand signals. A note hangs in the dressing room: 'Please do not touch the armband'. Nobody admits to writing it.
Scene: One hook for two
Before the match both armbands hang side by side on the hook, with a name tag and a little heart. Who drew it remains the dressing room's secret.
We saw nothing.
Yes, initiate him. With cake for everyone.
Cake for everyone! I'll find a baker right away.
Short and friendly. Without an audience.
Short and friendly. We'll sing quietly.
No. No games.
No games. All right. It was just a song.
Initiation for {spieler_kurz}
Coach, {spieler_kurz} has been here long enough. The squad wants to initiate him: sing a song, fetch cake, kiss the ball at the corner flag once. Harmless. We just wanted to ask first.
The cake was excellent. I lie gladly.
I asked for the recipe: petrol station, shelf four.
Nice. Training again tomorrow.
Tomorrow again. With a sugar rush.
The new boy sings
{spieler_kurz} survived the initiation. His song was wrong, loud and a hit anyway. The cake came from a petrol station, but nobody said so.
Do the initiation after all – briefly.
Briefly? I sing very briefly. Promise.
It stays a no.
Fine. He gets his song for his birthday.
{spieler_kurz} stays on the outside
Since the initiation was banned {spieler_kurz} sits a little apart at meals. Nobody is angry, but a song is missing. The skipper hums it while fetching coffee.
Scene: The late song
After the win someone starts the initiation song. {spieler_kurz} stands on the table and sings along. The kit man films, the physio cries a little.
I wasn't there.
Take a long weekend off.
A long weekend! I'll bring soup. For everyone.
We'll sit you with the countrymen.
That sounds good. I'll learn the card game.
It comes with the job. Tough it out.
Tough it out. With soup in my heart.
{spieler_kurz} misses home
Coach, I don't want to whine. But for days I've been dreaming of Grandma's soup, and the weather here doesn't help. I'm afraid it shows on the pitch.
I'll try some. Purely out of professional interest.
Professional interest with seconds. Understood.
Good to have you back.
Good to be back. And full.
Soup for everyone
{spieler_kurz} is back from home – with three pots. The dressing room smells of soup and contentment. The nutritionist doesn't change expression.
You get two days. Call your family.
Two days. I'll let Grandma's soup know.
Phone off. Concentration.
Phone off. Heavy-hearted.
{spieler_kurz} seems absent
{spieler_kurz} looks at his phone more than at the ball in training. The physio suspects homesickness, the kit man a new series. Both bad for passing accuracy.
Scene: The pot on the bus
On the away trip a pot travels through the bus. Everyone spoons, the driver politely declines but gets a bowl anyway. After the match he asks for the recipe.
Recipe enclosed.
You get the mirror. You water the plant yourself.
A cactus will do. It matches my aura.
The locker follows the performance.
Performance gets light. I take that as a bet.
A locker is a locker. No extras.
No extras. I'll remember that. In extra time.
{spieler_kurz} wants a locker of his own
Coach, no offence, but I need a locker with lighting. Really: a mirror, a spotlight, maybe a plant. If you play like I do, you want to live like it too.
I like the cactus. But time on the pitch counts.
Time on the pitch. The cactus will stand in if need be.
Good. Then show it in training.
I shine in training too. Without a spotlight.
The locker glows
{spieler_kurz} has furnished his locker himself: mirror, small spotlight, cactus called 'Gerald'. The squad secretly admires it and hides the fact.
Come on, let's find a solution. Cactus included.
Cactus included. That's something.
The decision stands.
It stands. And I stay in the corner.
{spieler_kurz} sulks
{spieler_kurz} has taken a corner spot in the dressing room, wearing headphones. The skipper says he would like to see scenes without premieres. The mood is theatrical.
Scene: Applause for the cactus
After the match a cactus stands at the press conference next to {spieler_kurz}. Nobody asks why. The cactus gets the best question of the day.
No comment.
There's a list. I'll pin it up.
A list! With order, numbers and a signature.
Whoever feels most certain takes it.
Everyone feels certain. That's the problem.
The captain decides. Full stop.
Full stop. I like that. The rest will learn.
Penalty row around {spieler_kurz}
Coach, we have a problem with penalties: {spieler_kurz} wants to take it, so does the regular taker, and yesterday the ball lay on the spot for two minutes. The referee smiled. We didn't.
Good list. Thanks for joining in.
Second is the new first. Officially.
As long as he scores.
He scores. Mostly. The list helps.
The list is up
On the board in the dressing room hangs the penalty list, ordered by nerves of steel. {spieler_kurz} is second and smiles as if it were first.
He scored. Next time he asks.
Next time I'll ask. Probably.
Ten euros in the kitty. For the coffee.
Ten euros. The coffee gets expensive.
The ball in the net – the wrong way
At the penalty {spieler_kurz} grabs the ball despite instructions and scores. The dressing room is divided: half cheering, half filing a complaint.
Scene: The team kitty
The team kitty fills up because everyone pays fines with pride. By the end of the season it covers a barbecue. The keeper gives the speech – mercifully short.
Cheers.
Good. Let the two practise together.
I'll put them at the same cone. What could go wrong?
Watch first, decide later.
I'll observe. With notepad and glasses.
The boy has to cope on his own.
Alone. Like in our day. Into the wind.
A godfather for {spieler_kurz}
Boss, {spieler_kurz} moves around in training like a deer on ice. The veteran centre-back has offered to take him under his wing. Sounds good, but I wanted to ask.
Tell both that I'm proud.
I'll tell them. The old one first – he'll blush.
Keep going, but no celebration.
No celebration. A small cake is fine.
The godfather delivers
{spieler_kurz} controlled the ball in training for the first time without looking round for the assistant coach. The veteran acts like it's nothing. It's everything.
Team up, you two.
We've already had coffee. The old man paid.
He'll sort it out himself.
Himself. He's taking courage with tea.
{spieler_kurz} broods
Without a godfather {spieler_kurz} looks like a tourist in training: friendly, lost, constantly holding a camera. The veteran watches from afar and sighs audibly.
Scene: Two rows of cones
After training the veteran and {spieler_kurz} stay on the pitch and rearrange cones. On the way to the dressing room you hear 'That wasn't bad' and 'Thanks, boss'.
A quiet moment.
You get a free afternoon.
A free afternoon! I'll sleep like a log. Standing up.
We'll shorten your sessions this week.
Shorter is good. Sleeping longer too.
This is pro sport. Carry on.
Carry on. I'll try – awake.
{spieler_kurz} is shattered
Coach, I admit it: I'm tired. Not physically – in my head. Yesterday I fell asleep on the bus and swung in a cross in my dream. It reached its man.
Great. I grant you every break.
Breaks are my new hobby. Thanks, Coach.
Good. Stay on track.
Track found. Even with a rear-view mirror.
The dormouse effect
After his free afternoon {spieler_kurz} is hard to stop in training. He even chased the ball he usually just politely escorted. The dressing room believes in a miracle.
Okay, you get your break after all.
A break! I swear I won't nod off. Almost.
Set yourself an alarm.
Alarm set. Five of them. Against sleep.
{spieler_kurz} nods off
During the tactics meeting {spieler_kurz} fell asleep with his eyes open for the first time in club history. The analyst notes 'Tactical line of sight: ceiling'.
Scene: The sleeping lion
At half-time {spieler_kurz} lies on the bench with his eyes closed and says: 'I'm gathering strength.' Ten minutes later he scores the goal of the game.
Don't tempt fate.
Come to the meetings. With tea.
With tea and notepad. I'm practically hired.
Get well first. Then meetings.
Well, then meetings. Order understood.
Rest. That's an order.
Rest. I'll count the flies on the ceiling.
{spieler_kurz} wants to be there
Coach, rehab is driving me mad. I've learned the exercise-bike wall by heart. May I at least come to the meetings? I'll bring tea too.
Good idea. Keep it up.
I even drew a sketch of the opponent. In colour.
Good. But don't forget the rehab.
I never forget rehab. It doesn't forget me.
The tea drinker on the bench
{spieler_kurz} sits in the front row at every meeting and takes notes. The analyst once asked whether he could bring figures too. He can.
Okay, come along. But no balls.
No balls. Promise. Except a small one.
You stay in the rehab room.
The room and I – a friendship.
{spieler_kurz} creeps round the dressing room
Since the order to rest {spieler_kurz} suddenly turns up everywhere: at the coffee machine, at the physio, once even on the bus. He says he just happened to pass.
Scene: The comeback in the team photo
In the team photo {spieler_kurz} stands in civvies in the back row and waves. In the picture it looks as if he'd scored the goal. The photo now hangs in the corridor.
Well hung.
Gladly. Drop by next week.
Next week. I'll bring papers and a biscuit.
Let's wait out the season.
Wait. I'll be impatient but polite.
I don't negotiate over rumours.
Rumours are my speciality. You'll hear.
{berater} calls about {spieler_kurz}
Good day, Coach. {berater} here. My client {spieler} is in demand and I hear things. Nothing concrete, but I wanted to sound out whether we should talk about his future before others do.
We agree: talk first, then see.
Talk first. Rarely has anyone said that.
Thanks for the talk.
My pleasure. I'll send the bill for the coffee.
{berater} drops by
{berater} sits with you for two hours, drinks three coffees and says 'just for information' ten times. He left with a handshake and the resolve not to sign anything.
I'll call back. We'll settle it calmly.
Calmly settle it. I'll fetch the paper as evidence.
Public statement. Today.
Today. With a photo if you like.
{berater} spreads rumours
The papers say {spieler} is 'unhappy and in demand'. The source: a 'well-informed circle' – three people, one of them {berater}. The press officer turns red.
Scene: The handshake in the corridor
In the corridor you meet {berater}. Both smile, both shake hands, both hold on a bit too long. The press officer decides to finish early today.
See you around.
Go ahead. But not a word to the press.
Not a word. The gummy-bear glue is already ordered.
Something smaller, please.
Something smaller. We'll use stickers then.
No. This is a club, not a circus.
Circus is nice too. But fine, Coach.
{spieler_kurz} is planning a prank
Coach, I'll be honest: {spieler_kurz} wants to glue your assistant's shoes to the floor. With gummy-bear glue, so harmless. We think it lifts the mood. But you decide.
Paid. The shoes too.
Thanks! The shoes were too tight anyway.
Enough. Back to training now.
Enough is enough. With glue in the cupboard.
The shoes hold
The assistant coach walked two metres yesterday and then no further. He laughed, then swore, then laughed again. Today he sends a counter-bill for a pair of shoes.
All right. One a month. Officially.
One a month! We'll keep minutes.
It stays that way.
It stays. Only secretly now.
The dressing room is silent
Since the ban a strange calm has settled over the dressing room. Someone wrote 'prank' on the board and wiped it off. The keeper still giggles quietly.
Scene: The counter-bill
On the dressing-room board hangs a bill: 'One pair of shoes, one pair of socks, nerves (flat rate)'. Underneath, the captain's signature and a small smiley.
File it.
